paper.abstract:
Abstract Pretrained diffusion models provide powerful image priors for training-free posterior sampling in image restoration. To guide this sampling process, frequency-aware methods progressively incorporate measurement information across frequency bands, facilitating coarse-to-fine reconstruction.
However, existing methods typically do not explicitly separate frequency activation from degradation-induced attenuation, leaving attenuation differences among inactive frequencies insufficiently modeled.
In this work, we propose frequency-decoupled posterior guidance to separate frequency activation from attenuation-aware spectral regularization.
Specifically, a progressive low-to-high frequency schedule determines the active measurement band, while a kernel-derived attenuation map defines a selective spectral prior over inactive components.
To stabilize the sampling process, we also introduce a local trajectory regularizer that suppresses spatially irregular state-to-clean deviations.
For a fixed endpoint energy, we provide a KL-regularized path-space interpretation. In practice, we construct time-dependent guidance through local energy corrections using a Tweedie plug-in approximation. Experiments on natural-image benchmarks demonstrate strong PSNR and SSIM performance across challenging non-blind deblurring settings, even at higher measurement noise levels.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Image restoration aims to recover a clean image from incomplete or corrupted measurements. A broad class of restoration tasks takes the form y = Ax 0 + n , n ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 0 , σ y 2 ​ I m ) , \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{A}\mathrm{x}_{0}+\mathrm{n},\qquad\mathrm{n}\sim\mathcal{N}\bigl(\mathrm{0},\sigma_{\mathrm{y}}^{2}\mathrm{I}_{m}\bigr), (1) where x 0 ∈ ℝ d \mathrm{x}_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} is the unknown image, y ∈ ℝ m \mathrm{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{m} is the observation, and A : ℝ d → ℝ m \mathrm{A}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{m} is a known linear operator. Recovering 𝐱 0 \mathbf{x}_{0} is generally ill-posed because operator A \mathrm{A} may attenuate or discard part of the image information. Effective restoration must therefore balance measurement fidelity with image priors. Classical methods design the prior through handcrafted regularizers, while more recent approaches use learned denoisers or energy models ( Rudin et al., 1992 ; Cai et al., 2012 ; Glowinski et al., 2017 ; Su and Huang, 2026 ; Roth and Black, 2005 ; Venkatakrishnan et al., 2013 ; Dong et al., 2015 ) . Diffusion models provide an expressive alternative by learning the score fields of progressively perturbed data distributions ( Ho et al., 2020 ; Song et al., 2021 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) . Conditional diffusion models can learn a direct degraded-to-clean mapping, but typically require paired data and task-specific training ( Saharia et al., 2022 ; Whang et al., 2022 ) . Zero-shot methods instead combine a pretrained unconditional diffusion model with the known forward operator at inference time ( Kawar et al., 2022 ; Song et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2023 ; Chung et al., 2023 ; Zhu et al., 2023 ) . This decoupling of the image prior from the observation model enables one pretrained model to address multiple inverse problems without retraining. Despite this flexibility, existing zero-shot methods commonly enforce measurement consistency through spatial residuals, pseudoinverse projections, or likelihood gradients ( Kawar et al., 2022 ; Wang et al., 2023 ; Chung et al., 2023 ; Meng and Kabashima, 2025 ) . For natural images, diffusion denoising often recovers coarse structure before fine detail ( Falck et al., 2025 ) . This behavior has motivated frequency-aware guidance, which progressively incorporates measurement information across frequency bands. FGPS follows this principle by gradually exposing measurement frequencies ( Thaker et al., 2025 ) ; noise-conditioned posterior continuation further couples frequency activation to the diffusion noise level ( Tian et al., 2026 ) . However, existing frequency-aware methods typically do not explicitly separate frequency activation from degradation-induced attenuation, leaving attenuation differences among inactive frequencies insufficiently modeled. This distinction matters for directional or frequency-selective blur, where frequencies at similar spatial scales can have substantially different responses. Motivated by these observations, we propose frequency-decoupled posterior guidance for non-blind image deblurring. By decoupling frequency activation from attenuation-aware regularization, our approach enables more precise incorporation of measurement information, effectively preventing highly attenuated or noisy frequencies from corrupting the update direction. Meanwhile, it better models inactive components by preventing the diffusion prior from introducing hallucination artifacts in spectral regions where measurement data is absent or severely degraded. Additionally, we introduce a local trajectory-stabilization regularizer that penalizes spatially irregular state-to-clean deviations, thereby promoting stable and spatially coherent sampling. Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We introduce frequency-decoupled diffusion guidance for non-blind image deblurring. It is realized via a progressive schedule that determines which measurement frequencies are active at each reverse step, along with a kernel-derived attenuation map that defines a selective spectral prior over inactive components. • We formulate these components in a time-dependent guidance energy and derive practical stepwise corrections using a Tweedie plug-in approximation. To stabilize the updates, we introduce a local trajectory regularizer that suppresses spatially irregular state-to-clean deviations. For a fixed endpoint energy, we also provide a KL/Gibbs path-space interpretation. • We evaluate the proposed framework on natural-image benchmarks across challenging non-blind deblurring settings. The method achieves strong PSNR and SSIM performance and remains robust as measurement noise increases. Controlled ablations clarify the roles of the individual components and identify trajectory stabilization as a key contributor to the observed improvements.

sections.heading: 3.1 Training-Based Diffusion Models for Image Restoration
sections.text: Conditional diffusion models learn restoration distributions from paired degraded and clean images. SR3 ( Saharia et al., 2023 ) conditions the reverse process on a low-resolution observation for image super-resolution, while Palette ( Saharia et al., 2022 ) extends conditional diffusion to a broader family of image-to-image tasks. I 2 SB ( Liu et al., 2023 ) , IR-SDE ( Luo et al., 2023 ) , and ResShift ( Yue et al., 2023 ) further incorporate the degradation process into the diffusion bridge or stochastic restoration dynamics. Their learned models or conditioning mechanisms are typically tied to the degradation distributions used in training.

sections.heading: 3.2 Training-Free Diffusion Methods for Inverse Problems
sections.text: A common training-free strategy keeps the pretrained diffusion model fixed and uses the known forward operator to guide sampling. Operator information and measurement guidance. DDRM ( Kawar et al., 2022 ) exploits the singular-vector structure of linear operators, while DDNM ( Wang et al., 2023 ) uses a range–null-space decomposition. DPS ( Chung et al., 2023 ) evaluates a likelihood surrogate at a denoised clean-image estimate; DMPS ( Meng and Kabashima, 2025 ) instead derives a closed-form likelihood-score approximation that avoids back-propagation through the denoiser. Frequency exposure and stabilization. A related line of work controls which frequency components are exposed to measurement consistency during sampling. FGPS ( Thaker et al., 2025 ) progressively exposes measurement frequencies during sampling. Noise-conditioned posterior continuation ( Tian et al., 2026 ) combines frequency exposure with a Haar-domain rule for committing coarse and detail corrections. MASF ( Qian et al., 2024 ) stabilizes generation by averaging frequency components of clean-image predictions across sampling steps. Our method uses kernel-derived attenuation to weight a spectral prior over inactive frequencies and regularizes state-to-clean deviations locally. Variational and reconstruction-oriented methods. Diffusion priors can also be incorporated into iterative reconstruction and explicit optimization objectives. DiffPIR ( Zhu et al., 2023 ) combines diffusion denoising with plug-and-play restoration, while RED-Diff ( Mardani et al., 2024 ) uses variational approximation and denoising regularization. DMAP ( Xu et al., 2025 ) reinterprets DPS through posterior maximization and combines multiple likelihood-ascent steps with projection onto the reverse-transition Gaussian shell to improve reconstruction performance.

sections.heading: Datasets and pretrained models.
sections.text: We evaluate on Flickr-Faces-HQ (FFHQ) ( Karras et al., 2021 ) and the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge 2012 (ILSVRC2012) validation set ( Deng et al., 2009 ; Russakovsky et al., 2015 ) , at 256 × 256 256\times 256 resolution. For each dataset–task setting, we use a fixed set of 1,000 1{,}000 evaluation images. Within each task, all methods receive identical degraded measurements for the same images. We use a pretrained unconditional diffusion model for FFHQ and a pretrained class-conditional model with ground-truth labels for ImageNet. The dataset-specific backbone is fixed across methods, without task-specific fine-tuning. Image preprocessing is detailed in Supplementary Sec. B . Our code will be available at https://github.com/Sea-serpents/frequency-decoupled-diffusion-guidance .

sections.heading: Tasks.
sections.text: We consider Gaussian, motion, and uniform non-blind deblurring, which exhibit isotropic, directional, and frequency-selective attenuation, respectively. Unless otherwise stated, measurements have additive Gaussian noise with σ y = 0.05 \sigma_{\mathrm{y}}=0.05 . Uniform deblurring uses a truncated forward operator. Kernel specifications, boundary conventions, and operator construction are given in Supplementary Sec. B .

sections.heading: Baselines and metrics.
sections.text: We compare with DPS ( Chung et al., 2023 ) , DSG ( Yang et al., 2024 ) , FGPS ( Thaker et al., 2025 ) , DPS-MAP ( Li and Wang, 2025 ) , and DMPS ( Meng and Kabashima, 2025 ) . We report PSNR and SSIM on RGB images in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] as the primary paired-fidelity metrics. LPIPS and FID results, together with their evaluation details, are provided in Supplementary Sec. C.1 .

sections.heading: Guidance and inference.
sections.text: We use ρ = 10 − 3 \rho=10^{-3} for the attenuation weight W κ W_{\kappa} , shared across RGB channels. Guidance coefficients follow sigmoid schedules, and the active-band cutoff follows an exponential schedule; their formulas and numerical settings are given in Supplementary Sec. B . Results labeled Ours fuse the outputs of two completed sampling branches: two base-guidance branches for Gaussian and motion blur, and a base branch with a CGJ-augmented branch for uniform blur. CGJ settings are shared across datasets; branch configurations and fusion weights are specified in the supplementary material.

sections.heading: Results on FFHQ
sections.text: Our method ranks first in both PSNR and SSIM for all three FFHQ tasks. Relative to the strongest competing result in each setting, it improves PSNR by 0.149 0.149 , 0.187 0.187 , and 0.231 0.231 dB for Gaussian, motion, and uniform deblurring, respectively. The improvement is therefore consistent across the three blur models and is largest under uniform deblurring, where the operator-specific CGJ branch is used. Compared with FGPS, which also uses a progressive frequency curriculum, our method improves PSNR by more than 2 2 dB and SSIM by at least 0.062 0.062 in every FFHQ setting. These results show that explicitly separating diffusion-time frequency activation from degradation-dependent spectral sensitivity substantially strengthens measurement-faithful reconstruction. sections.heading: Results on ImageNet.
sections.text: On the more diverse ImageNet dataset, our method remains within the top two for both fidelity metrics in every task. It achieves the best Gaussian deblurring result, exceeding DPS-MAP by 0.069 0.069 dB in PSNR and 0.003 0.003 in SSIM. Under uniform deblurring, the two methods are nearly tied in PSNR: our result is only 0.016 0.016 dB below DPS-MAP, while attaining the highest SSIM of 0.724 0.724 . Thus, although ImageNet motion deblurring remains a more challenging setting, the proposed guidance gives consistently strong fidelity across datasets and operators rather than being specialized to facial images.

sections.heading: 6 Conclusion
sections.text: In this paper, we introduced frequency-decoupled posterior guidance, a training-free framework that separates the diffusion-time activation of measurement frequencies from their reliability under the degradation operator. A progressive low-to-high schedule specifies the active measurement band, while a kernel-derived attenuation map weights the remaining inactive frequencies for spectral regularization. We provided a KL-regularized path-space interpretation of the fixed endpoint energy and derived practical stepwise guidance through a Tweedie plug-in approximation. Experiments on challenging non-blind deblurring tasks demonstrate consistent improvements in reconstruction fidelity and robustness to increased measurement noise. These results highlight the importance of jointly considering the evolving frequency content of reverse diffusion and the spectral properties of the degradation operator, and motivate further extensions to blind and nonlinear inverse problems as well as more efficient single-trajectory sampling. Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Guidance for Non-Blind Image Deblurring: Supplementary Materials This supplementary material provides theoretical proofs, experimental details, and additional analyses for the main paper. Section A presents the proofs of the path-space variational formula and the approximation error bounds. Section B details the datasets, degradation operators, method configurations, and baselines. Section C reports complementary perceptual metrics, complete component ablations, and two-branch inference analysis. Section D provides paired statistical comparisons. Section E analyzes hyperparameter sensitivity, Section F provides additional qualitative comparisons on FFHQ and ImageNet, and Section G reports detailed computational cost. Together, these results substantiate the theoretical claims and empirical effectiveness of the proposed method.

sections.heading: Appendix A Proofs
sections.text: In this subsection, we prove the path-space variational formula underlying the energy tilt and derive the resulting marginal score correction. We then quantify the error of evaluating the frequency-decoupled energy at a conditional mean. The first result is the Gibbs variational principle, also known as the relative-entropy variational formula; see, e.g., ( Donsker and Varadhan, 1975 ; Dupuis and Ellis, 1997 ) .

sections.heading: B.1 Datasets and Evaluation Protocol
sections.text: We evaluate on Flickr-Faces-HQ (FFHQ) ( Karras et al., 2021 ) and the ILSVRC2012 validation set ( Deng et al., 2009 ; Russakovsky et al., 2015 ) at 256 × 256 256\times 256 resolution. For each dataset–task setting, we use a fixed set of 1,000 1{,}000 evaluation images. Within each task, all methods receive the same degraded measurement of each image. Images are represented in RGB. FFHQ images are resized to 256 × 256 256\times 256 when necessary; ImageNet images are bicubically resized to 256 × 256 256\times 256 without cropping. For FFHQ, we use the pretrained unconditional ffhq_10m.pt checkpoint distributed with the official DPS release ( Chung et al., 2023 ) . For ImageNet, we use the pretrained 256 × 256 256\times 256 class-conditional diffusion checkpoint released with Guided Diffusion ( Dhariwal and Nichol, 2021 ) , conditioning on the ground-truth class labels. The backbone is fixed across methods within each dataset, without task-specific fine-tuning.

sections.heading: External assets and licenses.
sections.text: The FFHQ dataset resources are distributed under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license, while individual images retain their original Flickr licenses. ImageNet is used under its documented access terms for non-commercial research and educational purposes.

sections.heading: Sensitive content.
sections.text: FFHQ contains human face images and may therefore involve privacy-sensitive visual content. We use FFHQ solely as an image-restoration benchmark and do not perform identity recognition, demographic inference, or analysis of personal attributes. We do not collect or curate any new human-subject data. We compute PSNR and SSIM for each reconstructed image against its reference in RGB [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] and average the scores over the evaluation set. LPIPS is computed per image using the AlexNet backbone after mapping the reconstruction and reference to [ − 1 , 1 ] [-1,1] , and is averaged over the same set. FID is computed between the complete reconstructed and reference image sets; its implementation and the perceptual results are reported in Supplementary Sec. C.1 .

sections.heading: B.2 Degradation Operators
sections.text: We study Gaussian, motion, and uniform non-blind deblurring. Unless otherwise stated, the measurement follows Eq. ( 1 ) with additive Gaussian noise of standard deviation σ y = 0.05 \sigma_{\mathrm{y}}=0.05 . Each task uses the same realized measurements for all compared methods.

sections.heading: Gaussian deblurring.
sections.text: The blur kernel has size 61 × 61 61\times 61 and standard deviation 3.0 3.0 . The FFHQ forward operator uses zero padding, whereas the ImageNet operator uses reflection padding.

sections.heading: Motion deblurring.
sections.text: We use a 61 × 61 61\times 61 random-trajectory kernel generated once with intensity 0.5 0.5 and kernel seed 0 0 . It is fixed across the evaluated images and applied using zero-boundary convolution.

sections.heading: Uniform deblurring.
sections.text: The underlying kernel is a 9 × 9 9\times 9 uniform averaging kernel. The implemented forward operator uses a separable SVD construction with zero-boundary convolution. Specifically, let B \mathrm{B} be the one-dimensional zero-boundary convolution matrix for the nine-point averaging filter, and write B = U ​ diag ⁡ ( s i ) ​ V ⊤ \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{U}\operatorname{diag}(s_{i})\mathrm{V}^{\top} . Set B 0.03 = U diag ( s i 𝟏 { s i ≥ 0.03 } ) V ⊤ \mathrm{B}_{0.03}=\mathrm{U}\operatorname{diag}\bigl(s_{i}\mathbf{1}_{\{s_{i}\geq 0.03\}}\bigr)\mathrm{V}^{\top} and apply the separable operator A ⁡ ( X ) = B 0.03 ​ XB 0.03 ⊤ \mathrm{A}(\mathrm{X})=\mathrm{B}_{0.03}\mathrm{X}\mathrm{B}_{0.03}^{\top} independently to each color channel. Thus, singular values strictly below 0.03 0.03 are discarded in each one-dimensional factor before forming the two-dimensional operator. This truncated operator is used both to generate measurements and to evaluate measurement residuals. The attenuation weight W κ W_{\kappa} in Eq. ( 10 ) is instead computed from the Fourier response of the underlying 9 × 9 9\times 9 kernel. Thus, it serves as a kernel-based spectral proxy and is not the singular-value spectrum of the implemented forward operator.

sections.heading: B.4 Baseline Configurations
sections.text: We use public implementations of the five baselines with the same dataset-specific diffusion backbone, evaluation images, and degraded measurements as above. Their reverse-step counts and guidance settings are given separately because they differ across methods and tasks.

sections.heading: DPS.
sections.text: We run DPS ( Chung et al., 2023 ) for 1,000 1{,}000 DDPM reverse steps with guidance scale 0.3 0.3 . We use the released Gaussian and motion task configurations for FFHQ and ImageNet. sections.heading: DSG.
sections.text: We run DSG ( Yang et al., 2024 ) for 1,000 1{,}000 reverse steps. On ImageNet, we use the matched class-conditional backbone, retaining the guidance rule and frozen hyperparameters. sections.heading: FGPS.

sections.heading: DPS-MAP.

sections.heading: DMPS.

sections.heading: C.1 Complementary Perceptual Metrics
sections.text: Because our primary objective in non-blind image inverse problems is faithful recovery of the specific image associated with each measurement, we first report PSNR and SSIM in the main text. The complementary LPIPS and FID results are reported in Table 5 . The results reveal a clear separation between paired fidelity and perceptual quality. Although DPS-MAP and DMPS are among the strongest baselines in PSNR and SSIM, their LPIPS and FID values are frequently worse than those of FGPS and DSG, particularly on FFHQ. The main exception is ImageNet motion deblurring, where DPS-MAP achieves the best LPIPS and the second-best FID; DMPS also obtains a competitive LPIPS in this setting, although its FID remains high. Overall, FGPS achieves the best FID in all six settings and the best LPIPS in five of them, while DSG is generally the next strongest perceptual baseline. Our method does not dominate these perceptual metrics: its results often lie between the perception-oriented baselines and the strong distortion-oriented solvers, consistent with its emphasis on measurement-faithful recovery. These observations motivate reporting LPIPS and FID alongside, rather than in place of, the paired PSNR and SSIM results. Abstract Pretrained diffusion models provide powerful image priors for training-free posterior sampling in image restoration. To guide this sampling process, frequency-aware methods progressively incorporate measurement information across frequency bands, facilitating coarse-to-fine reconstruction. However, existing methods typically do not explicitly separate frequency activation from degradation-induced attenuation, leaving attenuation differences among inactive frequencies insufficiently modeled. In this work, we propose frequency-decoupled posterior guidance to separate frequency activation from attenuation-aware spectral regularization. Specifically, a progressive low-to-high frequency schedule determines the active measurement band, while a kernel-derived attenuation map defines a selective spectral prior over inactive components. To stabilize the sampling process, we also introduce a local trajectory regularizer that suppresses spatially irregular state-to-clean deviations. For a fixed endpoint energy, we provide a KL-regularized path-space interpretation. In practice, we construct time-dependent guidance through local energy corrections using a Tweedie plug-in approximation. Experiments on natural-image benchmarks demonstrate strong PSNR and SSIM performance across challenging non-blind deblurring settings, even at higher measurement noise levels. 1 Introduction Image restoration aims to recover a clean image from incomplete or corrupted measurements. A broad class of restoration tasks takes the form y = Ax 0 + n , n ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 0 , σ y 2 ​ I m ) , \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{A}\mathrm{x}_{0}+\mathrm{n},\qquad\mathrm{n}\sim\mathcal{N} igl(\mathrm{0},\sigma_{\mathrm{y}}^{2}\mathrm{I}_{m} igr), (1) where x 0 ∈ ℝ d \mathrm{x}_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} is the unknown image, y ∈ ℝ m \mathrm{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{m} is the observation, and A : ℝ d → ℝ m \mathrm{A}:\mathbb{R}^{d}	o\mathbb{R}^{m} is a known linear operator. Recovering 𝐱 0 \mathbf{x}_{0} is generally ill-posed because operator A \mathrm{A} may attenuate or discard part of the image information. Effective restoration must therefore balance measurement fidelity with image priors. Classical methods design the prior through handcrafted regularizers, while more recent approaches use learned denoisers or energy models ( Rudin et al., 1992 ; Cai et al., 2012 ; Glowinski et al., 2017 ; Su and Huang, 2026 ; Roth and Black, 2005 ; Venkatakrishnan et al., 2013 ; Dong et al., 2015 ) . Diffusion models provide an expressive alternative by learning the score fields of progressively perturbed data distributions ( Ho et al., 2020 ; Song et al., 2021 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) . Conditional diffusion models can learn a direct degraded-to-clean mapping, but typically require paired data and task-specific training ( Saharia et al., 2022 ; Whang et al., 2022 ) . Zero-shot methods instead combine a pretrained unconditional diffusion model with the known forward operator at inference time ( Kawar et al., 2022 ; Song et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2023 ; Chung et al., 2023 ; Zhu et al., 2023 ) . This decoupling of the image prior from the observation model enables one pretrained model to address multiple inverse problems without retraining. Despite this flexibility, existing zero-shot methods commonly enforce measurement consistency through spatial residuals, pseudoinverse projections, or likelihood gradients ( Kawar et al., 2022 ; Wang et al., 2023 ; Chung et al., 2023 ; Meng and Kabashima, 2025 ) . For natural images, diffusion denoising often recovers coarse structure before fine detail ( Falck et al., 2025 ) . This behavior has motivated frequency-aware guidance, which progressively incorporates measurement information across frequency bands. FGPS follows this principle by gradually exposing measurement frequencies ( Thaker et al., 2025 ) ; noise-conditioned posterior continuation further couples frequency activation to the diffusion noise level ( Tian et al., 2026 ) . However, existing frequency-aware methods typically do not explicitly separate frequency activation from degradation-induced attenuation, leaving attenuation differences among inactive frequencies insufficiently modeled. This distinction matters for directional or frequency-selective blur, where frequencies at similar spatial scales can have substantially different responses. Motivated by these observations, we propose frequency-decoupled posterior guidance for non-blind image deblurring. By decoupling frequency activation from attenuation-aware regularization, our approach enables more precise incorporation of measurement information, effectively preventing highly attenuated or noisy frequencies from corrupting the update direction. Meanwhile, it better models inactive components by preventing the diffusion prior from introducing hallucination artifacts in spectral regions where measurement data is absent or severely degraded. Additionally, we introduce a local trajectory-stabilization regularizer that penalizes spatially irregular state-to-clean deviations, thereby promoting stable and spatially coherent sampling. Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We introduce frequency-decoupled diffusion guidance for non-blind image deblurring. It is realized via a progressive schedule that determines which measurement frequencies are active at each reverse step, along with a kernel-derived attenuation map that defines a selective spectral prior over inactive components. • We formulate these components in a time-dependent guidance energy and derive practical stepwise corrections using a Tweedie plug-in approximation. To stabilize the updates, we introduce a local trajectory regularizer that suppresses spatially irregular state-to-clean deviations. For a fixed endpoint energy, we also provide a KL/Gibbs path-space interpretation. • We evaluate the proposed framework on natural-image benchmarks across challenging non-blind deblurring settings. The method achieves strong PSNR and SSIM performance and remains robust as measurement noise increases. Controlled ablations clarify the roles of the individual components and identify trajectory stabilization as a key contributor to the observed improvements. 2 Background 2.1 Notation We use ⊙ \odot for element-wise multiplication, I d \mathrm{I}_{d} for the d d -dimensional identity matrix, and 𝟏 Λ \mathbf{1}_{\Lambda} for the indicator function of a set Λ \Lambda . SR3 ( Saharia et al., 2023 ) conditions the reverse process on a low-resolution observation for image super-resolution, while Palette ( Saharia et al., 2022 ) extends conditional diffusion to a broader family of image-to-image tasks. I 2 SB ( Liu et al., 2023 ) , IR-SDE ( Luo et al., 2023 ) , and ResShift ( Yue et al., 2023 ) further incorporate the degradation process into the diffusion bridge or stochastic restoration dynamics. Their learned models or conditioning mechanisms are typically tied to the degradation distributions used in training. 3.2 Training-Free Diffusion Methods for Inverse Problems A common training-free strategy keeps the pretrained diffusion model fixed and uses the known forward operator to guide sampling. Operator information and measurement guidance. DDRM ( Kawar et al., 2022 ) exploits the singular-vector structure of linear operators, while DDNM ( Wang et al., 2023 ) uses a range–null-space decomposition. DPS ( Chung et al., 2023 ) evaluates a likelihood surrogate at a denoised clean-image estimate; DMPS ( Meng and Kabashima, 2025 ) instead derives a closed-form likelihood-score approximation that avoids back-propagation through the denoiser. Frequency exposure and stabilization. A related line of work controls which frequency components are exposed to measurement consistency during sampling. FGPS ( Thaker et al., 2025 ) progressively exposes measurement frequencies during sampling. Noise-conditioned posterior continuation ( Tian et al., 2026 ) combines frequency exposure with a Haar-domain rule for committing coarse and detail corrections. MASF ( Qian et al., 2024 ) stabilizes generation by averaging frequency components of clean-image predictions across sampling steps. Our method uses kernel-derived attenuation to weight a spectral prior over inactive frequencies and regularizes state-to-clean deviations locally. Variational and reconstruction-oriented methods. Diffusion priors can also be incorporated into iterative reconstruction and explicit optimization objectives. DiffPIR ( Zhu et al., 2023 ) combines diffusion denoising with plug-and-play restoration, while RED-Diff ( Mardani et al., 2024 ) uses variational approximation and denoising regularization. DMAP ( Xu et al., 2025 ) reinterprets DPS through posterior maximization and combines multiple likelihood-ascent steps with projection onto the reverse-transition Gaussian shell to improve reconstruction performance. 4 Method We propose a frequency-decoupled guidance framework for non-blind image deblurring.
